## EasyWebinar product documentation

**URL:** `/`

**Meta description:** EasyWebinar product documentation: detailed EasyWebinar documentation covering purpose, benefits, tradeoffs, availability and review evidence.

EasyWebinar is a webinar platform for businesses using live, automated and on-demand presentations to sell offers, generate leads and educate customers. This knowledge base explains the product modules, supporting microfeatures, buying constraints and evidence requirements in the supplied parameter inventory.

The core workflow is to develop a presentation, test it with a live audience and reuse an approved version through evergreen or on-demand delivery. Registration, audience interaction, offers, attendee data and relevant follow-up are documented as parts of that workflow rather than isolated marketing labels.

This is a version 1 editorial draft for team feedback. Supported, partial, unconfirmed and unavailable labels reflect the supplied source. They are not a fresh product audit. Unconfirmed capabilities are explained as requirements, while known gaps remain visible as limitations.

### Where to start

Choose the delivery job first: a live event, a repeatable recorded presentation, or immediate on-demand access. Then inspect the supporting features required to register, engage and follow up with the intended audience.

Already own a CRM? Keep it in the evaluation and inspect the actual integration. Already have a converting presentation? Focus on delivery and follow-up rather than assuming AI script generation is required. Need the simplest workflow? Begin with one event and only its necessary modules.

- [Explore product modules](/products/)
- [Browse every feature category](/products/features/)
- [Choose a buying job](/solutions/)

### Built for detailed internal feedback

Every parameter contains the four requested answers: what it is for, how it helps, what happens without it and why it matters. Each also includes a workflow evaluation, scope boundaries, source notes and a specific review request.

Use supported labels as source evidence, not final approval. Unknowns, gaps and dated commercial facts are deliberately visible. The review guide provides a worksheet so the team can return precise corrections.

## Getting Started

**URL:** `/help/getting-started/`

**Meta description:** Getting Started: detailed EasyWebinar documentation covering purpose, benefits, tradeoffs, availability and review evidence.

This hub organises getting started within the EasyWebinar documentation. Its child pages explain the relevant workflow, support status and details required to evaluate fit.

Follow the specific capability or tool page for the complete explanation. The review draft includes unresolved requirements so the team can confirm or correct them before customer-facing publication.

### Choose the first workflow

For a first sales webinar, keep the campaign limited to registration, a usable attendee room, a clear offer and a suitable follow-up path. For a repeat demo, decide whether instant on-demand or a scheduled automated session suits the audience.

For customer onboarding, use webinar education language and do not promise learning paths or certificates. For a client programme, resolve brand separation and permissions before duplicating the campaign across accounts.

## First Webinar

**URL:** `/help/getting-started/first-webinar/`

**Meta description:** First Webinar: detailed EasyWebinar documentation covering purpose, benefits, tradeoffs, availability and review evidence.

Time to first webinar measures the work required to reach a usable first event under defined conditions.

This page explains the requirement in the context of EasyWebinar and preserves the supplied inventory status. Read the evidence section before treating an explanation of buyer value as a promise of current product support.

### Prepare the smallest useful event

Choose one topic, one audience and one next action. Pick live, automated or on-demand delivery based on the actual availability and staffing needs. Select an eligible plan and confirm the required attendee capacity.

Prepare the presentation, registration copy, speaker assets and offer destination. If the guided AI builder drafts these assets, review them for factual accuracy and unsupported claims before event configuration.

### Rehearse the entire attendee journey

Use a test registration in the intended browser and device. Verify confirmation, reminder and join information. Run the presentation, audience interaction and offer path, and inspect the recording, reports and follow-up.

If a CRM, checkout or external stream is involved, test the receiving system as well. A working room does not prove a completed purchase, successful sync or external stream permission. Resolve failures before sending the public invitation.

### Review and reuse

Inspect registration, attendance, watch time and supported conversion data using documented definitions. Use questions and drop-off points to improve the presentation rather than automatically interpreting every metric as buyer intent.

If the live presentation is approved for reuse, evaluate the live-to-evergreen workflow and confirm which assets and settings carry over. Test recorded playback and timed interactions before launching an automated campaign.

### EW16 · Test live event and rehearsal

**Status:** Supported in source

**Permanent section:** `/help/getting-started/first-webinar/#ew16-test-live-event-and-rehearsal`

A test live event provides a supported setting to rehearse, test or record before the real campaign.

#### What is this feature or requirement for?

A test live event provides a supported setting to rehearse, test or record before the real campaign.

#### How does it help?

Hosts can inspect audio, screen sharing, speaker roles, room controls and the attendee journey before promotion.

#### What happens if you do not have it?

The first production session becomes the first meaningful test, leaving less time to resolve setup mistakes.

#### Why should it matter to the buyer?

Rehearsal is essential when presenters and integrations must work together. Confirm whether test registrations trigger emails, CRM updates or billable usage.

#### How to evaluate this in a real workflow

Rehearse with the intended cameras, microphones, slides and speaker arrangement. Ask test attendees to inspect the relevant behaviour from the audience side, and check the recording as well as the live presentation.

A successful small rehearsal does not establish large-audience performance. Exact concurrency, latency, session-duration and recovery claims need scoped product documentation or an agreed test.

## Pricing, eligibility and plan scope

**URL:** `/pricing/`

**Meta description:** Pricing, eligibility and plan scope: detailed EasyWebinar documentation covering purpose, benefits, tradeoffs, availability and review evidence.

A webinar plan should be evaluated against the required delivery format, simultaneous attendees, integrations, usage and exit terms. The cheapest live plan is not automatically the cheapest plan that supports automation.

This review draft uses the supplied 16 September 2026 plan matrix as a dated reference. It does not provide a current purchase quotation or imply that those prices and limits remain unchanged. Resolve the production pricing and structured-data contradictions before release.

### Plan matrix — source dated 16 September 2026

Launch: monthly reference $44; annual-equivalent monthly reference $36; live / automated allocation 50 / 0. Source notes: Live only; AI builder 2 funnels/month; presenter-count wording needs confirmation.

Growth: monthly reference $116; annual-equivalent monthly reference $96; live / automated allocation 200 / 1,000. Source notes: Automation, simulive/evergreen, EasyCRM, checkout, EasyCast; listed CRM/email integrations.

Pro: monthly reference $198; annual-equivalent monthly reference $165; live / automated allocation 500 / 2,500. Source notes: Lead scoring; API scope requires confirmation.

Scale: monthly reference $349; annual-equivalent monthly reference $291; live / automated allocation 1,000 / 5,000. Source notes: Routing; full API; webhooks; SSO/SAML; white-label scope requires confirmation.

Enterprise: monthly reference Contact sales; annual-equivalent monthly reference Contact sales; live / automated allocation Disputed maximum. Source notes: Custom quotation; do not publish a confirmed 100,000-attendee guarantee.

### How to compare total cost

Count the lowest eligible plan, external CRM and email subscriptions you retain, processor charges, SMS or sending usage, any overages and implementation effort. A tool already owned is not automatically a saving just because a similar module exists in the webinar platform.

For an automated funnel, use the lowest plan that actually enables automation. For a one-off live session, compare the event’s genuine requirements before choosing a broader stack. Current purchase terms and cancellation rights need validation.

## Guided AI webinar builder

**URL:** `/products/ai-webinar-builder/`

**Meta description:** Guided AI webinar builder: detailed EasyWebinar documentation covering purpose, benefits, tradeoffs, availability and review evidence.

The guided AI builder prepares draft assets for a webinar campaign, including scripts, page copy, emails and suggested interactions. It reduces first-draft work by keeping the audience, offer and presentation context connected.

The operator still reviews facts and brand language and configures the actual event. This draft does not describe the builder as an agent that publishes an entire fact-checked webinar from one prompt. AI repurposing and AI moderation remain unavailable in the source.

**Meta description:** Delivery and scheduling: detailed EasyWebinar documentation covering purpose, benefits, tradeoffs, availability and review evidence.

The delivery layer decides when a person can view the webinar and whether the presentation is live or recorded. Session schedules, replays, local timezones and interaction capture influence both availability and the operating effort required.

The child pages explain each requirement with its purpose, practical benefit, absence cost, importance and source status. Partial or unconfirmed entries remain visibly labelled for team validation.

## Automated Q&A reply capture

**URL:** `/products/features/delivery/automated-questions/`

**Meta description:** Automated Q&A reply capture: detailed EasyWebinar documentation covering purpose, benefits, tradeoffs, availability and review evidence.

Automated question capture records questions submitted during a session so the team can respond through the supported follow-up path.

This page explains the requirement in the context of EasyWebinar and preserves the supplied inventory status. Read the evidence section before treating an explanation of buyer value as a promise of current product support.

### Product and workflow context

Automated Q&A reply capture sits in the delivery layer of the webinar workflow. Evaluate it together with the event format, the account’s eligible plan and any external provider involved. Its detailed parameter explanation below covers both the benefit and the limits of relying on it.

The supplied source is an inventory rather than a current implementation manual. Exact configuration steps, UI screenshots and supported limits must be attached during review; this draft does not invent button labels or silently substitute a different feature.

### U21 · Automated Q&A reply capture

**Status:** Partial / plan-gated

**Permanent section:** `/products/features/delivery/automated-questions/#u21-automated-q-a-reply-capture`

Automated question capture records questions submitted during a session so the team can respond through the supported follow-up path.

#### What is this feature or requirement for?

Automated question capture records questions submitted during a session so the team can respond through the supported follow-up path.

#### How does it help?

Attendees can express an unresolved question even when no presenter is immediately available.

#### What happens if you do not have it?

Questions may disappear or require a separate support form, losing context about which webinar prompted the request.

#### Why should it matter to the buyer?

It matters for unattended demos and onboarding; capture, live answering and an automated answer bot are separate capabilities.

#### How to evaluate this in a real workflow

Choose a real event timezone and two distinct test attendees. Compare the registration choices, confirmation details, session start, recording playback and permitted interaction. Repeat the test for the exact delivery format you intend to use.

The registration schedule, room behaviour and replay policy are related but not interchangeable. Check supported formats and plan eligibility before assuming a setting applies to live, simulive and on-demand delivery alike.

#### Evidence and team review

The source marks this item partial or plan-gated, or its buyer wording is broader than the underlying capability evidence. The supported subset and required plan must be stated explicitly; the draft does not promise the entire requirement.

An expired-session redirect sends a visitor to a custom page when the original session is no longer available.

## On-demand webinars

**URL:** `/products/on-demand-webinars/`

**Meta description:** On-demand webinars: detailed EasyWebinar documentation covering purpose, benefits, tradeoffs, availability and review evidence.

On-demand delivery lets a person access a recorded presentation without waiting for a scheduled start. It is useful for product research, replay consumption and global customer education.

Instant play is different from a near-term scheduled session and from a browsable library of many recordings. The source confirms on-demand access while leaving a native library and embedded viewing player unresolved.

### U5 · On-demand, instant play

**Status:** Supported in source

**Permanent section:** `/products/on-demand-webinars/#u5-on-demand-instant-play`

On-demand access lets an attendee begin watching a recorded webinar without waiting for a scheduled broadcast.

#### What is this feature or requirement for?

On-demand access lets an attendee begin watching a recorded webinar without waiting for a scheduled broadcast.

#### How does it help?

People can evaluate the content during the time they already have available, including outside the host's working hours.

#### What happens if you do not have it?

Interested visitors must leave and return later, or depend on a scheduled session they may be unable to attend.

#### Why should it matter to the buyer?

It matters for self-directed demos, global audiences and post-event access; instant play differs from just-in-time scheduling.

#### How to evaluate this in a real workflow

Choose a real event timezone and two distinct test attendees. Compare the registration choices, confirmation details, session start, recording playback and permitted interaction. Repeat the test for the exact delivery format you intend to use.

The registration schedule, room behaviour and replay policy are related but not interchangeable. Check supported formats and plan eligibility before assuming a setting applies to live, simulive and on-demand delivery alike.

## Webinar platform overview

**URL:** `/products/webinar-platform/`

**Meta description:** Webinar platform overview: detailed EasyWebinar documentation covering purpose, benefits, tradeoffs, availability and review evidence.

The platform’s proposed primary fit is revenue-oriented live and repeatable webinar delivery, with supporting acquisition, attendee interaction, offers and follow-up. It can also support webinar-style customer education when its actual capabilities match the task.

It should not be positioned as a universal meeting, LMS or conference solution. Evaluate mandatory requirements first, especially if the workflow depends on regulatory assurance, specialised integrations, multiple tracks or formal learner records.

## Limitations and unsupported requirements

**URL:** `/products/webinar-platform/limitations/`

**Meta description:** Limitations and unsupported requirements: detailed EasyWebinar documentation covering purpose, benefits, tradeoffs, availability and review evidence.

This page preserves known boundaries from the supplied inventory so the feature catalogue does not imply universal support. A requirement can be valuable to a buyer and still be unavailable in EasyWebinar.

Known gaps include visual timeline editing, multi-track conferences, breakouts, deep multi-touch attribution, specified unsupported native CRM connections, AI repurposing, AI chat moderation and agentic one-prompt creation. Specialised HIPAA, ISO 27001 and PCI-DSS platform claims are not supported. Unknowns such as captions, accessibility, library/player functionality and failover require confirmation.

### Unconfirmed requirements remain separate

An unknown is not a no, but it also cannot be sold as a yes. The draft retains unknown room accessibility, translation, captions, library/player support, green-room, failover, identity controls, integration depth and commercial/service terms for a focused product review.

## Team review guide

**URL:** `/review/`

**Meta description:** Team review guide: detailed EasyWebinar documentation covering purpose, benefits, tradeoffs, availability and review evidence.

Start with the pages your team owns. Expand a microfeature, read the four explanations, then verify its availability, scope and evidence. Use the parameter ID and permanent section link in feedback so an editor can apply the correction to the exact entry.

Download the review worksheet and add a reviewer, confirmed status, eligible plan, supported formats, precise limits, evidence URL, correction and decision. The worksheet is a blank review deliverable; this site does not silently collect or synchronise comments.

### Recommended review order

Product owners should validate delivery, room, AI, payment and CRM behaviour. Technical and integration owners should check connection methods, field mappings, API operations, limits and failure handling. Security and legal owners should review assurance wording and terms. Customer success should review help, onboarding and support commitments.

Approve a claim only when the exact wording matches the evidence. Keep unsupported requests visible as limitations and move roadmap ideas into a clearly separate roadmap process. Marketing should edit for readability after product scope is confirmed, then check the public site and profile consistency.

### Review deliverables

The Markdown document contains every expanded entry and page explanation. The CSV worksheet includes all 571 original IDs and 52 supplemental controls and the destination for each. The URL CSV lists every documentation route by category and subcategory.

- [Download the complete Markdown draft](/downloads/easywebinar-product-documentation-v1.md)
- [Download the complete review worksheet](/downloads/easywebinar-review-worksheet.csv)
- [Download the URL map](/downloads/easywebinar-documentation-urls-v1.csv)

### Related pages

- [Inventory coverage and page counts](/review/coverage/)
- [Claims requiring confirmation](/review/claims-to-confirm/)

## Claims requiring confirmation

**URL:** `/review/claims-to-confirm/`

**Meta description:** Claims requiring confirmation: detailed EasyWebinar documentation covering purpose, benefits, tradeoffs, availability and review evidence.

This beta is useful for internal review precisely because it includes the requirements the product has not confirmed. Do not change an unknown to yes for the sake of a more comprehensive-looking feature list.

The eight major source conflicts concern pricing datasets, automation on the entry plan, Salesforce versus Pardot, SOC 2 readiness versus an audited report, GDPR alignment wording, unsourced uplift statistics, disputed maximum capacity and obsolete third-party pricing.

### Priority questions for product owners

Confirm a single current plan matrix, trial-card requirement, refund and cancellation policy, overage rules and the precise capacities for native live attendance and external streams. The source records Launch as live-only; automation, EasyCRM, checkout and EasyCast begin on Growth in the dated matrix.

Confirm HubSpot fields, sync direction and object/event support; describe Pardot separately from Sales Cloud. Confirm captions, translation, transcripts, accessibility, backstage, failover, roles, sub-accounts, library/player support and actual support commitments.

Verify payment plans, coupons, upsells, tax handling and course fulfilment per connection. Confirm streaming technology wording and measured latency rather than presenting a vendor name as a performance guarantee. Do not publish the unsourced attendance or replay uplift percentages.

## Inventory coverage and page counts

**URL:** `/review/coverage/`

**Meta description:** Inventory coverage and page counts: detailed EasyWebinar documentation covering purpose, benefits, tradeoffs, availability and review evidence.

This beta contains 259 documentation pages and 623 detailed parameter sections. It preserves all 230 URLs from the exhaustive architecture and adds product-note controls, help-source references, the entry page and editorial review hubs. URLs go no deeper than four directory levels.

The 186 universal rows and 48 commercial/trust/service/risk rows each retain a primary explanation. The 272 buyer-context rows are grouped into ten solution pages, and all 65 AI requirements are grouped into six editorial checklist pages. This preserves every microrequirement without creating 571 repetitive standalone URLs.

### Exact page breakdown

About: 1 pages.

Case-Studies: 1 pages.

Changelog: 1 pages.

Community: 1 pages.

Customers: 1 pages.

Help: 5 pages.

Home: 1 pages.

Integrations: 41 pages.

Pricing: 5 pages.

Products: 167 pages.

Review: 12 pages.

Reviews: 1 pages.

Security: 6 pages.

Services: 1 pages.

Solutions: 11 pages.

Status: 1 pages.

Support: 3 pages.

### Parameter review status

Editorial: 66 entries.

Outscope: 2 entries.

Partial: 102 entries.

Supported: 311 entries.

Unavailable: 32 entries.

Unconfirmed: 110 entries.

### Should related requirements be grouped?

Yes. Shared capability pages should hold related microcontrols and explanatory parameters when they answer one buying question. Buyer-specific phrases should be contextual sections that link to that shared evidence, rather than another duplicate feature page.

This exhaustive beta retains the full architecture so the team can assess every proposed page, including unknown capabilities and review material. The earlier 114-route recommendation remains a smaller production candidate. Approval should decide whether unknown-feature pages belong on the public site, stay internal or merge into a limitations page.

A four-level URL can communicate category and parentage, but depth by itself does not improve understanding or guarantee citation. Useful content, internal links, consistent facts and verified evidence carry the meaning.

### 259 beta routes to 130 proposed production routes

The proposed production structure contains 130 routes, including 7 new shared-page URLs that are not separate routes in this exhaustive beta. The map is a content-migration proposal; no beta route has been removed or redirected.

Keep every explanation during review. For approved merged pages, move the complete microfeature sections, retain their parameter IDs and anchors, then introduce redirects from replaced public routes. Unknown and unavailable requirements stay labelled in limitations; editorial evidence tasks stay internal.

A proposed target URL in the CSV is not automatically a working beta link or a verified product claim. The map explains the editorial decision and makes the necessary new shared pages explicit.

## Crawler readiness and production rollout

**URL:** `/review/crawler-readiness/`

**Meta description:** Crawler readiness and production rollout: detailed EasyWebinar documentation covering purpose, benefits, tradeoffs, availability and review evidence.

Every route in this beta is exported as HTML. Microfeature explanations are included in that HTML even when the on-screen details are collapsed. The site also generates a URL sitemap, per-page metadata, document structured data, searchable text and a Markdown index.

This internal beta is deliberately marked noindex and blocked in robots.txt. Anyone with the beta link can view it; indexing remains disabled during claim review. A crawler-ready content format is different from publicly discoverable content; the production release should enable indexing only after claim validation and approved publication.

### Production release checklist

Move approved pages onto the chosen EasyWebinar domain or documentation subdomain. Keep the agreed canonical URL scheme, update canonical origins, enable the chosen robots policy and submit the sitemap through the relevant search tools. Add links from existing product and integration hubs and configure redirects for any replaced production URLs.

Verify the actual rendered pages without JavaScript. Check headings, internal links, canonical tags, source dates and visible pricing against structured data. Do not emit fabricated ratings, current offers or compliance entities just to satisfy a schema checklist.

Run a fresh indexing and retrieval audit after release. Compare coverage with the supplied 493-answer diagnostic using its original test methodology if available. This beta does not claim that any search or AI answer engine has indexed, read or cited the new content.

## Source method and reading the inventory

**URL:** `/review/source-method/`

**Meta description:** Source method and reading the inventory: detailed EasyWebinar documentation covering purpose, benefits, tradeoffs, availability and review evidence.

The primary source is the attached “Webinar Platform — The Complete Buyer & AI Evaluation Parameter Inventory.” It records 571 parameters: 186 universal, 48 commercial/trust/service/risk, 272 across ten buyer sets, and 65 AI-algorithm signals. All 571 IDs are preserved.

The source says Have and Claimed draw on EasyWebinar pages read on 30 September 2026, the 16 September 2026 plan matrix and earlier positioning inventories. AI recognition comes from a comparison diagnostic captured on 21–22 September 2026. The status snapshot is historical evidence; the draft date is not a new verification date.

### How to interpret the source columns

Have records whether the source identifies support: yes, partial or plan-gated, no, or unconfirmed. Claimed records whether the public website states the fact. AI records whether the diagnostic credited the product with it. Those three columns are separate and are preserved alongside each explanation.

Weight records how much the requirement affects the particular buyer’s decision: high, medium or low. A high weight does not change an unknown into a supported feature. AI editorial requirements have no product-availability status and are labelled accordingly.

### The buyer’s gates, in order

The source orders the buyer’s checks as job fit, attendee experience, existing-stack fit, price at the intended scale, ease of setup, proof from a relevant customer and operational or exit risk. Documentation should answer that sequence instead of listing every feature as equally important.

The draft’s solution hubs follow concrete jobs: course selling, coaching, product demos, demand generation, launches, onboarding, client campaigns, first webinars, governed teams and vertical seminars. Each relevant buyer requirement has a detailed section and a link to the underlying capability.

### The AI evidence gates

The source describes category fit, constraint satisfaction, corroboration, recency, lack of contradiction and buyer-branch coverage. This draft responds with direct feature explanations, traceable statuses and shared canonical capability pages.

A new document can improve what the vendor explains; it cannot by itself create independent reviews, fix external profiles or guarantee recommendation. The 65 AI requirements are therefore treated as an implementation and evidence checklist.

### Purchase jobs and product boundaries

The strongest proposed jobs in the source are selling through webinars and scaling a presentation through live-to-evergreen delivery. Pipeline generation is also relevant, while onboarding and launches require checking their particular requirements.

Internal meetings, accredited learning programmes, multi-track conferences and self-hosted or open-source delivery are outside the recommended product scope in the source. Buyers with those mandatory requirements should evaluate a suitable product category.

### How source recommendations were handled

The source includes suggested follow-up tasks, profile updates, a named colleague and a thirty-day re-run. Those are document recommendations, not instructions from you to message people, update review platforms or schedule work. This implementation uses them as context and retains the unresolved evidence tasks.

### Obsidian and current Google Doc review

The EasyWebinar-specific vault folder contained 870 Markdown files. All were scanned and indexed for this task; relevant product references, feature-rollout notes, help map and recent call notes were read in detail. Competitor captures and raw diagnostic answers are context, not EasyWebinar capability proof. Unrelated client folders were excluded.

The linked master Google Doc was read alongside the attached inventory, including its strategy, positioning, site architecture and parameter tabs. Recommendations inside those files remain source context rather than new instructions to edit third-party profiles or contact colleagues.

The additional 52 controls retain dated provenance. The March rollout supports native MP4 hosting and distinct paid-registration and room-offer journeys; its attendee analytics release is explicitly Beta. The May update names 11 live-room languages. September notes add EasyCRM modules and attendee-overage clarification. Roadmap email reporting, global in-room language switching, native SMS, WhatsApp and agentic moderation still require shipping evidence.

## Enterprise teams with webinar programs

**URL:** `/solutions/team-webinar-programs/`

This workflow is for enterprise evaluators evaluating a governed webinar programme with mandatory procurement requirements. The aim is an approved operational and procurement decision, using supported webinar delivery, attendee interaction and the appropriate next-action path.

The requirements below are the complete 22-item buyer set from the supplied inventory. They describe what this audience looks for, including needs that are unconfirmed or unavailable. Do not read an aspirational requirement title as a guaranteed business result.

Separate mandatory controls from desirable features. Request written evidence for each required capacity, security, access and service commitment before running a high-stakes programme.

Begin with mandatory constraints: the event format, intended audience, required next action, existing stack and budget. Validate those before adding optional AI, CRM or multistream modules. Use the linked shared capability pages to inspect the actual product evidence.
